# `Q-19-1` — Plot Document Not Found

> The hephaestus plot document (`.hep`) an image refers to could not be read.

## What this means

An image in the document points at a hephaestus plot document — a
file ending in `.hep` — and Quarto could not read that file. Quarto
renders `.hep` files to SVG at render time so every HTML page shows
the plot; when the file cannot be read there is nothing to render, so
the image is left exactly as written and the rest of the page still
renders. The browser then shows a broken image where the plot should
be.

The message names the path as written and the location it resolved
to.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **The path is wrong.** A relative path is resolved against the
  directory of the document that contains the image, not the
  project root. A path starting with `/` is resolved against the
  project root.
- **The file was never written.** A code cell that was expected to
  produce the plot did not run, failed, or wrote the file somewhere
  else (for example under a different `fig-path`).
- **The file is not readable** because of permissions, or it was
  deleted or renamed after the reference was written.

## How to fix

Check the resolved location the message reports against where the
file actually is, then fix the path or move the file. For a plot
produced by a code cell, look for an earlier error from that cell.

## Related errors

- [`Q-5-6`](../project/Q-5-6.qmd) — Referenced Resource Not Found. A
  missing `.hep` raises both: this code says the plot was not rendered,
  `Q-5-6` says the file could not be copied into the output alongside
  the page, as for any missing image.
